title: The Weeping Wax Saint
text: One morning a wax saint stands in the square, weeping real tears. Pilgrims come from three valleys. So do the flies, which are wrong; each has a tiny human face.

options.label: Let the pilgrims come, and take their coin for the Commons.

outcomes.text: Candles and coin fill the square. The saint weeps on, and the flies stay close.
Each day the saint's face softens a little. One morning it wears the face of a Scion of the city, who has felt watched ever since.

options.label: Melt the wax saint down to learn what is inside it.

outcomes.text: The wax screams as it runs. In the pool at the bottom lies an old, gilded human skull. The faithful do not forgive it.
The wax will not melt. For three days the fire under it will not go out, and it takes a House's outbuilding with it.

options.label: Sell it to the Apostate traders, who have asked twice, and let them carry it off.

outcomes.text: They pay well and ask nothing. The flies follow the cart out of the city, then come back one by one.
